transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-25
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Ally Wong (CSM); Priya Shah (Head of ML Infra, NexaMed), Daniel Lopez (CTO), Evan Murphy (SRE)

Optional auto-summary (auto): Quick sync on Dedicated sizing after last week's steady-state tests; main focus is autoscale policy and burst planning.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we we have about 45 minutes so we'll go over the numbers you sent and then propose a Dedicated config and autoscale policy. quick check, is everyone good on audio?
00:08 Priya: yeah all good, thanks Samir.
00:12 Marco: cool, i'll share my screen in a second, but quick recap — last week you sent the 7-day histogram and the 10-minute spike captures, right Priya?
00:20 Priya: yes, uploaded to the folder under /nexameds/poc/traffic. there are two big spikes — one at 11pm UTC and another at 03:00 UTC, both short lived about 8-12 minutes.
00:30 Samir: perfect. can you summarize expected SLOs again? i have p99 target 200ms for the core inference route?
00:36 Priya: correct. p50 can be lower, but p99 needs to be ~200ms or better, and p95 around 80ms.
00:44 Marco: okay that helps. quick note — our p99 includes network + model time; if you want stricter p99 we usually recommend pre-warmed warm-pool capacity or an aggressive burst pool.
00:55 Evan: when you say warm pool, do you mean GPUs pre-warmed with KV cache? how long to warm?
01:00 Marco: right, we warm the model and keep the KV in GPU memory. warm time depends on the model and sequence length, typically 15-40 seconds to fully prime the cache for long contexts; shorter for short contexts. so for very spiky traffic you want a small warm pool to handle spikes without cold starts.
01:16 Daniel: what's the trade-off cost-wise for keeping a warm pool?
01:20 Samir: it's a steady cost — think of it as reserved capacity you keep online. we recommended a burst pool size in the spreadsheet based on your peak QPS. we can also do auto-burst where the platform will pull from burst capacity before spinning new nodes, reduces p99 but costs more during bursts.
01:34 Priya: what's the recommended baseline? our median QPS is approx 120, 95th is 420, and peaks to ~820 for short bursts (about 10 minutes).
01:44 Marco: thanks, that distribution is helpful. with those numbers we suggest an initial Dedicated pool: min nodes = 2, target steady nodes = 4, max nodes = 10, burst pool = 3-4 nodes pre-warmed. that translates to roughly 4 x A100 equivalents steady and ability to burst up to 10 nodes.
01:58 Evan: A100 equivalents, ok. can you give the rough per-node QPS for your runner?
02:04 Marco: ballpark — depends on model and sequence length. for your 1k token average sequence we measured ~70-110 qps per A100 for the model variant you ran. so 4 nodes gives 280-440 qps sustained, which matches your 95th. the burst pool handles the 820 spikes.
02:20 Priya: that seems reasonable. what about autoscaling triggers? utilization or queue-length?
02:24 Marco: we recommend a hybrid policy. primary scale-up trigger: queue length > 30 requests for 30s or GPU util > 70% for 60s. scale-down: GPU util < 30% for 120s and queue empty. the reason is GPU util alone can be noisy because batching changes it; queue length gives a direct signal for latency pressure.
02:43 Daniel: how fast can we scale up? time to spin a node and warm the model?
02:47 Samir: spinning a fresh node to readiness is ~90-180s depending on image and model size. warming KV cache is additional 20-40s. that's why burst pool and pre-warming is important for those sub-3 minute spikes.
02:59 Evan: can we have a small cold-start pool where nodes are partially initialized?
03:03 Marco: yeah, that's warm vs cold concept. we support a pre-warm image that keeps the container and model loaded but not KV filled; warm pool has KV. pre-warmed nodes reduce spin + warm to maybe 40-60s. we can model costs for a mix: 2 pre-warm, 3 warm, then autoscale extra nodes as needed.
03:18 Priya: what's the recommended max for safety? we don't want runaway costs if a bug spikes traffic.
03:22 Samir: set an upper bound (max nodes) with auto-scaling caps, and we can set budget-based policies that stop scaling over a daily spend threshold and alert your team. also integrate route-level throttles.
03:34 Evan: any recommended fallbacks? like degrade model size or route to hosted?
03:37 Marco: yes we typically recommend a fallback chain: try primary model variant, if scale limit reached then route to a smaller quantized variant (lower latency, higher perf) and then as last resort fallback to Redwood hosted endpoints with lower SLO but unlimited scale. we can wire automatic routing policies.
03:51 Daniel: ok, about the model variants — you saw our test results where the quantized 4-bit gave worse quality on certain prompts. is it safe to auto-route?
03:59 Marco: fair point. automatic fallback should be opt-in for routes where quality regression is acceptable. for core clinical inference you probably want to avoid automatic quantized fallback; instead use canary-based manual escalation or A/B rollouts.
04:12 Priya: agreed. we'll limit auto-fallback to non-critical routes.
04:16 Samir: on cost — i ran a quick model of estimated monthly cost for the suggested baseline (steady 4 nodes + 3 warm pool burst occasionally). monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go: a 12-month reserved commit gives about 20-30% off internal unit costs. i'll put the full numbers in the spreadsheet.
04:30 Priya: thanks, yes please include both hourly burn and 30-day peak scenarios.
04:34 Marco: one operational note — monitor KV cache hit rate and effective batch size. Higher batch sizes reduce per-token cost but increase latency variance. for your p99 objective we recommended limiting batch window to 25-40ms while still enabling dynamic batching.
04:49 Evan: do you expose per-token cost breakdown and per-route costs in the console?
04:53 Ally: yes we do. Console has token-level cost, per-route latency, and you can export CSVs for billing. we'll share a demo link after this call.
05:00 Priya: security — any notes about private deployment or VPC connectivity for this POC?
05:04 Samir: for Dedicated we can run in your VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS. for POC we used hosted but we can spin a Private Dedicated trial in your VPC for the next phase if compliance needs it.
05:15 Daniel: do you have SOC2 or ISO stuff? our security team will need the evidence.
05:18 Ally: yes SOC2 Type II available, ISO pending on some docs; i'll attach the compliance pack.
05:24 Priya: also need audit logs retention options — how long do you keep request logs by default?
05:28 Samir: default 30 days, add-on retention available to 1-7 years depending on your plan. we'll note that in the security docs.
05:35 Priya: perfect.
05:37 Marco: quick check on the benchmark we ran on Wednesday — we saw a median latency of 55ms, p95 120ms, p99 230ms at 400 qps steady across 4 nodes; at burst 820 we saw p99 spike to ~600ms without warm pool, with a warm pool of 3 nodes p99 came down to 180ms.
05:57 Priya: that matches our runs, we saw similar numbers. so warm pool of 3 is important.
06:02 Samir: based on that, recommendation: min 2 nodes, steady 4 nodes (A100 equiv), warm pool 3 nodes, max 10 nodes, pre-warm 2. Autoscale triggers: queue-based scale-up + util guardrails. Budget cap and fallback chain to smaller model (manual opt-in).
06:19 Daniel: what about burst billing? are bursts billed at higher rates?
06:22 Samir: same per-node burn; bursts just mean you pay for more nodes during that window. no hidden surge premium, but we can bill differently if you want committed burst credits.
06:30 Evan: how do we test failover to hosted endpoints? will it preserve request context?
06:34 Marco: routing preserves request metadata but quality/SLO will vary. we recommend synthetic failover tests during quiet periods to validate behavior.
06:42 Priya: ok let's talk timeline — we want to finalize Dedicated size and get a trial in our VPC by the end of September.
06:48 Samir: doable. immediate next steps: Samir sends sizing spreadsheet, Marco runs 1-hour test, Priya uploads histograms. we reconvene after test results.
06:57 Ally: i'll send calendar invite for the follow-up and attach the docs.
07:00 Samir: anything else?
07:02 Daniel: one small ask — can you include an example autoscale policy YAML for our infra team to review?
07:07 Marco: sure, i'll paste a sample policy in the notes.
07:11 Priya: thanks all.
07:13 Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
07:15 [call ends]

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cache appear as K-V cash in auto transcript), speaker tags sometimes simplified; manual review recommended for compliance docs.
